<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/package.json`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via buildMcpBridge (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/package.json`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (symbol, 57 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **38** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1bed8536bba1bd59e432e7b9d8ebc3c526efc637` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b9f7a7b462cf4974e169e887662daf226dffeb04` — the merge of head `fbdba0708e50558dd62890d05508f4132ae9b0c3` into base `1bed8536bba1bd59e432e7b9d8ebc3c526efc637`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b9f7a7b462cf4974e169e887662daf226dffeb04 && git checkout b9f7a7b462cf4974e169e887662daf226dffeb04
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1bed8536bba1bd59e432e7b9d8ebc3c526efc637 fbdba0708e50558dd62890d05508f4132ae9b0c3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1bed8536bba1bd59e432e7b9d8ebc3c526efc637 && git merge --no-ff fbdba0708e50558dd62890d05508f4132ae9b0c3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1bed8536bba1bd59e432e7b9d8ebc3c526efc637
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1bed8536bba1bd59e432e7b9d8ebc3c526efc637` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `95b340e227301d6981ca67295c46c58724e43ae6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: hits — MCP `validate_expression` (`/api/v1/mcp` `tools/call` and stdio) at `site: 'validation'` / `'formula'`; `@objectstack/lint` root exports; `McpDataBridge.servedObjectDefinitionOf`; `@objectstack/mcp` runtime dependency set; the served `SKILL.md` line. Implementing files — `packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`, `packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`, `ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts`, `packages/mcp/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `turbo.json`, and the tests (`authored-site-expression.test.ts`, `mcp-validate-expression.test.ts`, the two mcp bridge-member ledgers, the two `packages/runtime` bridge tests).

Read: card #32872 body and all 5 comments (claim 6855829217, amendments 6856483394 and 6857864931, os-dev-report 6858983583), PR #33134 body, the net diff `9433d4f3..95b340e2` (19 files, +799/−31) and the files at the head. Check-runs on the head at 16:43Z: 63 total, 23 success, 9 skipped, 31 in progress, 0 failed. Still running: Build Core, Test Core 1–8/8, Test UI 1–16/16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI, Lint · PM dispatch-gates. Completed green include Check Changeset, Validate Package Dependencies, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate. No test or type-check verdict exists yet for this head; this record does not stand in for one.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Tool refusals at `validation` — right.** Unguarded nullable operand, `parent` read, hop to a field the target does not declare, hop into a stored-metadata table (errors), and the unprovisioned-anchor warning. Each is a finding the gate's own rule loop and `check` produce on the same rule (`validate-expressions.ts` rule loop, lines 3543–3618 at the head). Narrowing only: `ok` becomes `result.ok && gate.errors.length === 0`; nothing the tool refused before is now accepted.
2. **Tool refusals at `formula` — right.** The two hop refusals and the anchor warning, from `judgeFieldFormula`. No null guard and no `parent` verdict there, as at the gate.
3. **`flow_condition` / `template` unchanged — right as a derived judgment, wrong as stated** (see ④ F2): the tool's verdict there does not move, but the gate does not judge a flow condition with the shared validator alone.
4. **Hop-target reads are a new disclosure — wrong, undeclared** (④ F1, must-fix). The tool now answers, per probed column, whether a `sys_*` object declares a field, with `allowSystemObjects` off. That is a widening of what the tool reveals on a PR declared as narrowing only.
5. **New lint exports** `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression`, `authoredExpressionHopTargets`, `AUTHORED_RULE_NAME`, `AUTHORED_FORMULA_FIELD_NAME`, types `AuthoredSiteExpression`, `AuthoredExpressionSite` (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — right, additive, on the root entry only. `runStackExpressionPasses` and `StackExpressionOptions` stay off all three package entries.
6. **New gate option `sharedValidatorRunByCaller`** — right. It cannot reach a gate run (④).
7. **New optional bridge member `servedObjectDefinitionOf`** — right, additive on an exported interface; an implementer without it keeps the old verdict. Both in-repo bridges serve the read `describeObject` projects.
8. **`@objectstack/lint` becomes a runtime dependency of `@objectstack/mcp`** — right as a dependency (no cycle; a published-package change the changeset states). The way it is loaded is ④ F4.
9. **Response shape** — the added findings are `{ source, message }` with no `code`; validator findings keep theirs. Additive, stated in the PR's Acceptance notes. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/32872-validate-expression-gate-parity.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@object-ui/console`. The four packages are exactly the ones whose published source moves. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value or type an author may write changes, and the gate's acceptance set is untouched. Under AGENTS.md "the level follows the kind alone", `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. Both are present (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`); the disposition's reason holds for every refusal judged right in ①.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: the arm is right for ① 1–2. It is incomplete for ① 4: the same handler also reveals more than it did (F1). Fixing F1 by guarding the targets restores the declaration as written.
- The Clause-② sentence ends "no exported type or signature changes". False as written: `McpDataBridge` gains a member, lint gains six names, `StackExpressionOptions` gains one. All additive, and the changeset's own bullets list them. Reword to "no existing exported type or signature changes" in both the PR body and the changeset (nit, F5).
- `Skills-docs: none`: holds. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md:201` and `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md:484` say only that the tool runs the build's validator.
- Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **os-dev-report `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`.** Not accepted: F1 is a security-relevant behaviour the report does not name. Escalated as must-fix.
- **Dev landing note, #33108 (formula-cycle pass).** Answered with a condition, escalated to the seat's landing step. At 16:43Z `origin/main` (`5c005e0e`) carries no change to `validate-expressions.ts`, `mcp-http-tools.ts`, `skill-md.ts` or lint's `index.ts` since the merge base, so #33108 has not landed. If it lands first, the formula pin reds **only if** its call is a bare call inside `judgeFieldFormula` or in the few lines between the `judgeFieldFormula(...)` call and the `// [#26646]` marker. A call placed anywhere else (after the objects loop, beside `bulkConfirmTextIssues`, or as a member call) leaves the pin green and the tool silently short of the gate. The seat must read where #33108's call sits when merging main, not rely on the pin. Classification when it lands: `pass-silent-here` is the honest one (no authored field can reference `__validate_expression__`, so the probe is never in a cycle), with the limitation written down: the tool cannot give the cycle verdict because it is not handed the field's name.
- **Findings carry no `code`** — accepted (① 9).
- **Probe rule named `this rule`, probe field `__validate_expression__`** — accepted. The null-guard and `parent` sentences read "validation rule 'this rule'", which is intelligible and stated in the changeset.
- **Hint lists still come from the tool's own index** — accepted, out of this card.
- **The shared validator runs once** — accepted, with the consequence named in ④: the validator half of the verdict agrees with the gate by a parallel hint, not by construction.
- **Card member 3 measured rather than read from source** — done by the dev (PR "Measurement on origin/main"); accepted on the PR's evidence, not re-run here.
- **Claim amendments** (package.json, ledgers, turbo.json, cross-package inputs): the diff stays inside the amended file surface. No breach.

### ④ Design judgment

**F1 — must-fix. Hop targets bypass the tool's system-object fence.** `packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts:gatePassFindings` (line 1804) calls `bridge.servedObjectDefinitionOf(target)` for every reference target the expression reads through, with no `guard(target)`. `guard` is "the fail-closed object-name guard shared by every object-scoped tool"; with `allowSystemObjects` off (the default) `describe_object('sys_user')` and `validate_expression({ objectName: 'sys_user' })` are refused ("is a system object and is not exposed via MCP"), and `list_objects` filters `sys_*` at the tool layer, which shows the bridge does serve them. After this diff, `validate_expression({ objectName: <any object with a reference to sys_user>, expression: 'record.owner.X > 1', site: 'validation' })` answers `unknown field X on sys_user` or stays clean, one bit per probed column, to a `data:read`-scoped caller. The read is still the caller's ADR-0106 projection, so no FLS-masked field is confirmed; what is breached is the MCP tool-layer fence, and bridge-level `describeObject` parity is not tool-level `describe_object` parity. No test covers a `sys_*` hop target (`mcp-validate-expression.test.ts:290` pins the subject only). Fix, either: (a) skip a target `guard` refuses, as an unserved target is skipped, add the pin, and say in the SKILL line and changeset that hops into system objects are judged only with `allowSystemObjects`; or (b) keep the read and obtain a ruling that this oracle is acceptable, then declare it and pin it. (a) is the fail-closed default and keeps `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` true. Read from source, not run.

**F2 — should-fix. "A flow condition is judged by the shared validator alone, as at the gate" is false.** At a flow condition the gate's `check` also runs `warnUnprovisionedAnchors` (`validate-expressions.ts:2670`, "provenance rides every object-bound predicate"), and on a record-triggered flow's start, `decision` and edge conditions it runs `checkFlowNullGuards` → `checkNullGuards` at severity `error` (lines 3017, 3152, 3257, 3387). So `validate_expression({ site: 'flow_condition', triggerKind: 'record_change', expression: 'days > 3' })` still answers `ok: true` where the publish gate refuses. That is outside this card's two sites, so it does not fail the narrowing, but the sentence ships in the changeset (published CHANGELOG), the PR body, the `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP` docblock (`mcp-http-tools.ts:1719`) and a test title (`mcp-validate-expression.test.ts:554`), and the SKILL line lists the unprovisioned-column warning without a site. Correct the four sentences to "not judged by this change", qualify the SKILL warning to the two sites, and file the follow-up card for the flow members; card #32872 calls itself the closing card for the family, and it is not.

**F3 — should-fix. The enumeration pin fails for a narrower set of additions than the card asks.** `authored-site-expression.test.ts:SITE_REGIONS` scans four source regions for bare calls. It reds for a bare call added inside `check`, the rule loop, `judgeFieldFormula`, or the short span after its call site. It stays green for a member call, and for a pass added anywhere else in the walk that judges a rule or a formula field (whole-stack passes of the `bulkConfirmTextIssues` shape already exist at the walk's tail). A pass in the walk located on `objects[0].validations[0].` or on the probe field's `where` is carried by construction regardless, so the exposed case is a pass located elsewhere or needing input the tool lacks. State the pin's reach in the test header, and widen it (for example, classify every top-level `issues.push(...fn(` of `runStackExpressionPasses`). See the #33108 flag in ③.

**F4 — should-fix. Static import of lint's root barrel at MCP module load.** `mcp-http-tools.ts:92` imports `@objectstack/lint` statically. Every other server-side consumer reaches lint through `@objectstack/lint/runtime` and loads the root lazily (`metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts`: "the kernel boot path reaches `@objectstack/lint` only through its `/runtime` entry"; `build-probes.ts`). Lint builds with `splitting: false`, so a host that already loaded `dist/runtime.js` now also parses a second self-contained `dist/index.js` (552,936 B by lint's own `runtime.ts` header) at boot. The PR's "no host gains a package it did not already load" is true per package and misses the entry. `typescript`, `sucrase` and `ajv` stay lazy (`lazy-deps.test.ts`), so this is cost, not breakage. Fix: `await import('@objectstack/lint')` inside `gatePassFindings`, which is already async.

**F5 — nit.** Clause-② sentence wording (②).

**F6 — nit.** `storedExpressionInputIssues` is classified `pass-silent-here`. Honest for a `formula` probe, but a stored (non-`formula`) field's `expression` authored through `site: 'formula'` gets the gate's stored-input warnings and none from the tool. Name it in the follow-up card of F2.

**F7 — nit. Context the one-object probe stack does not share with the gate.** Each is a corner to write down; the first two are the only ones where the tool refuses and the gate does not:
- Package closure: the object save door narrows `objects` to the written package's closure (`runtime-gate.ts:narrowObjectsToWriteClosure`), so a target outside it is not judged there; the tool judges any target the caller is served. The tool's refusal is true (the field does not exist), the door's silence is the gap.
- A target field masked from the caller is refused as undeclared. Conformant with ADR-0106 D1 and with what the shared validator already answers for a masked subject field.
- A target the caller is not served is not judged, so the tool stays `ok` where the gate refuses. Residual, in the pre-existing direction.
- A picklist-bound field is served with resolved `options`; a default option makes it non-nullable for the tool while the authored body the gate reads names only the picklist. Tool accepts, gate may refuse an ordering comparison on it.
- `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` finds the subject by `o.name === objectName`; on the bridge's no-protocol fallback (`getObject(name)`) a differently-spelled name would answer `[]` silently.
- A fault-tier target now turns the call into a door error instead of a verdict. Same answer `describe_object` gives for that target.

**F8 — nit.** "No gate caller passes `sharedValidatorRunByCaller`" rests on a grep in the PR body. A source-scan pin that the one passer is `authored-site-expression.ts` would hold it by test.

Questions asked, answered:

- **Agrees with the gate verdict for verdict, by construction?** For the gate's own passes at both sites, yes: `judgeAuthoredSiteExpression` runs `runStackExpressionPasses` itself over a stack of the subject plus hop targets with `runtimeWriteType: 'object'`, and filters by the rule's key path or the probe field's `where`. No pass is copied. For the validator half, no: the tool keeps its own `validateExpression` call with a hint it builds from `describeObject`, and the gate's call is skipped. That half is parity by parallel construction, pre-existing (#32817, #32870), not regressed here. Subject to F1 and the F7 corners.
- **Can `sharedValidatorRunByCaller` weaken a gate run?** No. `runStackExpressionPasses` has three callers at the head: `validateStackExpressions` passes `{}`, `authoring-rules.ts:827` passes the literal `{ runtimeWriteType: ctx.runtimeWriteType }`, and the new entry. Neither gate caller spreads caller-supplied options. The option is read with `=== true`, and the type and the function are on none of lint's three `exports` entries, so no package consumer can pass it. Absent, both replaced expressions evaluate the original call unchanged.
- **Does the probe stack lose context?** Extensions are already folded into a served definition; stored-metadata hops are judged from the subject's own reference fields plus a static table check, so they need no target definition; injected system columns are stripped with `stripInjectedSystemColumns`, the exact inverse of the `governServedItem` injection the served read applies, and the walk re-derives them. The differences are the F7 list.
- **Is `servedObjectDefinitionOf` caller-scoped?** At the bridge, yes: runtime returns `readObjectForCaller(name)`, the same masked read behind `describeObject` and `optionFieldsOf`, and `mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts` adds it to the ADR-0106 case table (hidden, fault, masked field set). Stdio reads `servedView.getObject`. The definition is rendered to nobody and the gate's messages name only the caller's own input and the served names. At the tool, no: F1.
- **Does the pin fail when a gate pass is added?** Inside its four regions as a bare call, yes; otherwise no (F3).
- **SKILL.md line and mirror.** Byte-identical: the `validate_expression` bullet extracted from both files at the head compares equal (20 lines). True for the two sites on a bridge that serves the member, with the F1 and F2 corrections owed.
- **Lint as a runtime dependency.** No cycle: lint depends on `formula`, `metadata-core`, `sdui-parser`, `spec`, none of which depends on mcp. mcp publishes `dist` with dependencies external, and the lockfile move is the matching six lines. Validate Package Dependencies is green. Load shape: F4.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-wqhn19`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8a5f028fb9865775568c14a1b4faf7dbbe836cb5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: round 2, delta `95b340e2..8a5f028f` of the round-1 scope. Hits — MCP `validate_expression` at `site: 'validation'` / `'formula'` (HTTP and stdio), `@objectstack/lint` root exports, `McpDataBridge.servedObjectDefinitionOf`, the `@objectstack/mcp` runtime dependency, the served `SKILL.md` line. Merges `c00b9afc` (main, #33108) and `8a5f028f` (main, #33142) read for interaction only.

Read: fix commit `e306a89d`, classification commit `bd2b25ff`, the files at the head, the rewritten PR body, the round-2 os-dev-report 6863007477 on card #32872. The PR's net diff against main is still the same 19 files (+1006/−36). Check-runs on the head at 19:40Z: 67 total, 14 success, 11 skipped, 42 in progress, 0 failed. Still running: Build Core, Build Docs, Test Core 1–8/8, Test UI 1–16/16, all Type Check jobs (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger, UI), all Lint jobs (ESLint, repo & tooling, docs & code guards, CI/release/engine, the three scoped ones, PM dispatch-gates, UI), Live E2E UI, Build & E2E UI. No test, type-check or lint verdict exists yet for this head. This PASS is the contract judgment on the diff; it does not stand in for those runs, and the seat reads them before landing.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Refusals at `validation` and `formula` — right, unchanged from round 1.** The entry (`authored-site-expression.ts`) and the gate option are byte-identical to `95b340e2`; only main's #33108 adds lines to `validate-expressions.ts`.
2. **Hop-target disclosure — now right.** `mcp-http-tools.ts:gatePassFindings` takes `exposed`, bound at the call site to `guard(name) === undefined`, and skips a target before `bridge.servedObjectDefinitionOf(target)` is called. With `allowSystemObjects` off, a `sys_*` target is neither read nor judged; with it on, it is judged, as `describe_object` would describe it. The declaration `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is true again.
3. **Formula-cycle pass (#33108) at the formula site — right as classified.** `formulaCycleIssues` locates each finding on a cycle member's own `expression`; the entry keeps only findings on the probe's `where`. Detail in ④.
4. **`flow_condition` / `template` — right and now stated truthfully.** Unchanged verdict; the gate's own passes there are named as not run.
5. **Lint loaded lazily — right.** `import type` at module top, `await import('@objectstack/lint')` inside `gatePassFindings` after the subject is found. Same shape as `metadata-protocol`'s lazy root loads.
6. Lint exports, the gate option, the optional bridge member and the runtime dependency: as judged right in round 1, unchanged.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset unchanged in level: `patch` on `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@object-ui/console`; `Metadata-protocol: none`; BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` kept. Correct under AGENTS.md ("the level follows the kind alone").
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds with F1 fixed. The sentence now reads "no existing exported type or signature changes" in both the PR body and the changeset (F5 fixed).
- `Skills-docs: none` still holds.
- The changeset now states the hop-target fence, the lazy load and the internal gate option. Check Changeset had not completed on this head at the read.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Round-2 report `security_findings: "withheld"`.** The report names no finding and gives no carrier. Round 1's F1 is the one security-relevant item this review found, and it is fixed in the diff. Escalated to the seat: ask the dev what is withheld and where it was reported before landing; this review found nothing further.
- **Round-2 `out_of_scope_findings` (three).** Accepted as stated, all for one follow-up card the seat files: (a) `flow_condition` parity (null-guard gate on record-triggered flow conditions, unprovisioned-anchor warning); (b) a stored non-`formula` field's `expression` authored through `site: 'formula'`; (c) the cycle verdict for the formula being authored. The card is owed before #32872 closes, since the PR body now says it "closes #32872 at the two sites the card names" and points at that follow-up.
- **#33108 landing note from round 1.** Resolved.
